# Wait-ZbxHost

## SYNOPSIS

Waits until a host exists on the server.

## SYNTAX

```
Wait-ZbxHost [-Name] <string> [-Timeout <TimeSpan>] [-Interval <TimeSpan>] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

The Wait-ZbxHost cmdlet polls host.get every -Interval until a host with the technical name in -Name exists, and writes it; after -Timeout (two minutes by default) it stops with an error. It is the companion of autoregistration: an active agent's first autoregistration attempt fails by design and the host appears after the agent's next refresh, so a script that starts an agent waits for its host before configuring it. It needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Wait for a host an agent registers

```powershell
Wait-ZbxHost -Name 'web-01' -Timeout '2m' | Select-Object TechnicalName, HostId
```

Writes the host as soon as it exists; here web-01 exists already, so it returns at once.

### Example 2: Wait for a new host, then configure it

```powershell
$null = New-ZbxHost -Host 'web-02' -Group 'Web servers' -InterfaceType Agent -InterfaceIp '10.0.0.12'
Wait-ZbxHost -Name 'web-02' -Interval '5s' | Add-ZbxHostGroupMember -Group 'Linux servers'
```

-Interval sets how often to look; the pipeline continues with the host once it is there.
